latin.249:
ANNOTATIO IV.
De Obicibus Consociationis Ecclesiasticae ad pag. 341. 343.
latin.250:
§. I.
Post tot Pacis Ecclesiasticae componendae molimina frustrata, non immeritò in OBICES, Conatibus tam piis oppositos, inquirit Autor P. 341. & seq. ad speciales tamen digitum solùmmodò intendens, generalioribus, ex quibus isti derivantur, silentio praetervectis, quos intereà & ipsos summarium saltem memorâsse è re fuerit, eum potissimum in finem, quò studiosius caveantur.
latin.251: Herciscimus a. eos in Externos, seu extra hominem positos, & in Internos, seu homini domesticos.
latin.252: Priores variis Diaboli, mendaciorum, rixarum ac calumniarum parentis primi instinctibus, technis artibusque nefariis comprehenduntur, uti neutiquam cum vulgo, omnia propemodum malefacta sua horumque culpam in Diabolum transferre solito, supramodum exaggerandis, ita neque cum fascinati Mundi Autore vel rerum vel actionum humanarum Communitate eximendis:
latin.253: Quandoquidem ab ipso Spiritu S. dissidiorum non minus ac calumniarum, quam homicidiorum ex istis pullulantium, Pater, Diabolus nuncupatur Joh. 8. 44. non hominibus duntaxat inhians, Leonis rugientis ad instar 1. Pet. 5. adque opera sua incitans, Jacob. 4. quin permittente ex justo judicio Deô, operationem etiam suam in filiis infidelitatis perque eos peragens, Eph. 2, 2. collat. cum 5, 6. inque Judam etiam aliquem, Proditorem Christi, illapsus, Joh. 13; sed rixas insuper in specie excitans, alens, promovensque; ob id, respectu primae earum scaturiginis, denominandas Diabolicas. Jac. 3, 15. hincque tritico Veritatis ac Pacis, Mendaciorum ac Dissidiorum Zizania interferens.
latin.254: Ut Proinde quaesituro: Quis molimina Pacis supra recensita demolitus sit, haud ineptè verbis Christi respondeas: πονηρὸν Inimicumque communem id perpetrâsse, Matth. 13, 28.

pass_a.249:
ANNOTATION IV.
On the Obstacles of Ecclesiastical Consociation, at pages 341–343.
pass_a.250: §. I. After so many frustrated Efforts of composing Ecclesiastical Peace, the Author not undeservedly inquires into the OBSTACLES opposed to attempts so pious, p. 341 and following — yet pointing only at the special ones, the more general ones from which those are derived having been passed over in silence, which it will meanwhile have been worthwhile at least to have mentioned in summary, chiefly to this end, that they may be more carefully guarded against.
pass_a.251: We divide them (a) into Externals, or those placed outside the man, and into Internals, or those domestic to the man.
pass_a.252: The former are comprehended under the various instincts, devices, and nefarious arts of the Devil, the first parent of lies, quarrels, and calumnies — so that they are neither to be exaggerated beyond measure with the common crowd accustomed to transfer nearly all its misdeeds and their blame onto the Devil, nor, with the Author of the fascinated World, to be exempted from the Community of human things or actions:
pass_a.253: Seeing that by the Holy Spirit Himself the Devil is named Father of dissensions no less than of calumnies and of the homicides sprouting from them, John 8:44 — not only gaping after men like a roaring Lion, 1 Peter 5, and stirring them to his works, James 4, but also, God permitting by just judgment, carrying out his operation in the sons of unbelief and through them, Ephesians 2:2 compared with 5:6, and even having entered into some Judas, betrayer of Christ, John 13; but moreover exciting, feeding, and promoting quarrels in kind; on that account, with respect to their first spring, to be named Diabolical, James 3:15; and hence sowing the tares of Lies and Dissensions among the wheat of Truth and Peace.
pass_a.254: So then to one asking: Who demolished the peace Efforts recounted above, you would not unaptly answer with Christ’s words: that the wicked one and common Enemy did it, Matthew 13:28.

249: On the Obstacles to Ecclesiastical Consociation (Autor pp. 341–343).
250: §. I. After so many frustrated attempts to compose church peace, the Author not without cause turns to the OBSTACLES set against such pious efforts (p. 341ff.).
He points only at the special ones, passing the more general sources in silence — yet it is worth at least summarizing those generals too, mainly so they may be more carefully guarded against.
251: We divide them, first, into Externals — placed outside the person — and Internals — at home in the person.
252: The external sort fall under the Devil’s varied instincts, tricks, and wicked arts — he being the first parent of lies, quarrels, and slanders.
We must neither exaggerate with the crowd that dumps nearly every misdeed on the Devil, nor, with the author of this fascinated world, exempt him from the community of human things and deeds.
253: For the Holy Spirit Himself names the Devil father of dissensions no less than of slanders and of the murders that sprout from them (John 8:44).

He does not only gape after people like a roaring lion (1 Peter 5) and spur them to his works (James 4); God permitting by just judgment, he also works in the sons of unbelief and through them (Ephesians 2:2 with 5:6), and even entered a Judas, betrayer of Christ (John 13).

Moreover he stirs up, feeds, and pushes quarrels of that kind — so, from their first spring, they are rightly called diabolical (James 3:15) — sowing tares of lies and dissension in the wheat of truth and peace.
254: So to anyone who asks who wrecked the peace attempts recounted above, you may aptly answer with Christ’s words:
the wicked one — our common enemy — did it (Matthew 13:28).
Stop before §. II (internal fountains: pravity of will and error of intellect).
